mesh._defaults_note: cfg / dense_steps / eta were relying on the generation script argparse defaults (7.0 / 50 / 300.0) — the values below are those defaults written out, so behaviour is unchanged. They are here because a run config that omits them hides which knobs were never explored: cfg in particular had never been set for any domain, while sp_cfg was deliberately lowered 7.0 -> 5.0, so the two stages were guided at different strengths without that being visible anywhere.
mesh._hidden_defaults_note: These were live but invisible: the generation script has ~104 CLI knobs that no run config set, so their argparse defaults silently decided behaviour. Only the ones ACTIVE under this config's own gates are written out here, at their effective values, so this is a no-op. Gates: reach_* need cw>0; sp_guide_w_peak needs sp_guide_w>0; sp_lap_sigma needs sp_lap_w>0; sp_thick_target needs sp_thick_w>0; sp_rmin_void_weight needs sp_rmin_w>0; sp_normal_fd_* need sp_normal_fd_w>0; lambda_*/mu_aug_lag/inner_steps need aug_lag; beta_*/eta_bisect_iter need heaviside_proj; fea_mesh_* need fea_w>0. Two are worth a second look: reach_iters=100 caps the reachable path at 100 voxels while the 64^3 diagonal is 111, and sp_guide_w_peak=80 is 8x the sp_guide_w=10 the configs set, i.e. the schedule peak was never chosen deliberately.
mesh._disabled_losses_note: Inventory of loss terms that are IMPLEMENTED but disabled. They were invisible before: the weight defaulted to 0.0 in argparse and no config mentioned them, so a reader could not tell the capability existed. Values here are the effective ones (0.0), so this is a no-op — it is an inventory, not a change. Two are directly applicable to a fixed brake caliper and worth turning on: (a) sw + symmetry_axis=1 — reflection IoU about Y is 98.7% (domain), 98.3% (bores), 100.0% (lugs), while about X it is only 68.7% because the lugs sit on the -x face alone, so symmetry_axis must be 1, NOT the default 0 (=X). (b) sp_overhang_w for castability. The tw family (tw / tw_hard / tw_soft with min_thick) is NOT usable on this part: it measures thickness on the 64^3 grid where one voxel is 3.181 mm, but the delivered median wall is 3.00 mm = 0.94 voxel, i.e. below the grid it would be measured on, and min_thick=3 means 9.54 mm which would force the part solid. Thickness has to be handled by sp_thick_w / sp_thick_target on the sparse 512^3 stage instead. vw is deliberately 0: aug_lag already imposes V <= vol_target as an inequality, so vw would duplicate it.
